correctness.rationale: The proof fixes \(s=d/2>0\), constructs two coordinate slices, and shows that axis strictness makes the maximal transverse radii tend to zero with slice width. The two slice constraints then force both components of the common direction below an arbitrarily small bound, contradicting its required near-unit norm. Coordinate functionals are norm one for the dual absolute norm, and regrouping gives the arbitrary-family \(\ell_p\) corollary. No computation substitutes for the analytic argument.

originality.rationale: The full 2018 endpoint paper and the 2020 quantitative paper were inspected at the relevant definitions and direct-sum results. The former proves only the endpoint \(d=2\) obstruction; the latter defines \(\mathrm{SSD}(d)\mathrm P\) and gives direct-sum results for \(s\)-ASQ rather than the claimed all-positive-\(d\) obstruction. Dedicated searches found no statement implying the theorem. The one-way implication \(s\)-ASQ \(\Rightarrow\) \(\mathrm{SSD}(2s)\mathrm P\) specifically prevents the published \(s\)-ASQ failure from covering the present conclusion.
residual_risks: Terminology-divergent, unindexed, or inaccessible literature could contain an equivalent quantitative obstruction; the searches and inspected primary texts did not reveal one.

value.rationale: The endpoint theorem only rules out \(d=2\). The accepted claim proves a complete collapse of every positive quantitative level for a natural geometric class of absolute norms, including all \(\ell_p\)-sums with \(p<\infty\), independently of the factors. It resolves a genuine quantitative gap rather than renaming the endpoint result.
